fields.appearance: Māgha Pūrṇimā, about the middle of the 15th century Śaka, at Kheturī
fields.disappearance: Kārtika Kṛṣṇa Pañcamī (Gauḍīya calendar), merged into the Gaṅgā at Gambhilā
fields.works: Prārthanā, Prema-bhakti-candrikā, many songs; Bengali verse of the Smaraṇa-maṅgala; the Garāṇhāṭī kīrtana (Hāṭa-pattana and others attributed to him are doubtful)
fields.notes:
Son of Rājā Kṛṣṇānanda Datta, kāyastha zamindar of Gopālapura (capital Kheturī, Rajshahi), and Nārāyaṇī Devī; cousin of Santoṣa Datta. Received at twelve the prema the Lord had left in the Padmā (Prematalī). Left home on the Kārtika pūrṇimā; Lokanātha Gosvāmī's only disciple (dīkṣā on the Śrāvaṇa pūrṇimā), after secretly cleaning his master's place every night; studied under Jīva Gosvāmī, who gave him the title Ṭhākura. Lifelong brahmacārī. Organised the Kheturī festival (six Deities; first Gaura-pūrṇimā). Āśrama at Bhajana-ṭuli. Disciples include Santoṣa Datta, Rāmakṛṣṇa Ācārya, Gaṅgānārāyaṇa Cakravartī, Jagannātha Ācārya, Rājā Narasiṁha and Rūpanārāyaṇa. Dearest friend: Rāmacandra Kavirāja.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Campaka-mañjarī; also held to be a manifestation of Nityānanda.

fields.aka: Duḥkhī Kṛṣṇadāsa, Śyāmānanda Prabhu, Duḥkhī, Kṛṣṇadāsa
fields.place: Born at Dhārendā-Bāhādurpur (Daṇḍeśvara, Orissa); preached in Orissa from Nṛsiṁhapura and Gopīvallabhapura (Rādhā-Govinda); samādhi at Gopīvallabhapura, puṣpa-samādhi in Vṛndāvana
fields.notes: Son of Kṛṣṇa Maṇḍala and Durikā Devī, sadgopas. Disciple of Hṛdaya Caitanya at Ambikā-Kālnā (who named him Kṛṣṇadāsa); studied under Jīva Gosvāmī with Śrīnivāsa and Narottama. Found Śrī Rādhā's anklet while cleaning the groves in Vṛndāvana; She marked his forehead with it and named him Śyāmānanda — the tilaka of his line. In 1582 carried the Gosvāmīs' books to Bengal with Śrīnivāsa and Narottama; revived the faith in Orissa; converted many Muslims. Foremost disciple: Rasikānanda (Rasika Murāri). Called a manifestation of Advaita Ācārya. Left this world in 1630 at Nṛsiṁhapura, in the house of Uddaṇḍa Rāya Bhuiyān. His Deities: Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Śyāmasundara (Vṛndāvana).
